literal: Moon and five planets offending listed lodges and classical fixed stars changing; appended sightings recorded.
idiomatic: Transits of the moon and five planets against lunar lodges and principal fixed stars, with appended anomaly records.

literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu fourth year, third month, guimao: the moon offended the great star of Heart.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangchu under Wei Emperor Wen, on the guimao day of the third lunar month, the moon transgressed the principal star of the Heart mansion.

literal: The prognostication text says, "Heart is the throne-seat of the celestial king; the king abhors it.
idiomatic: The divination reads, "Heart marks the ruler’s celestial throne; the sovereign dreads such an omen.

literal: " In the sixth month, jiashen, Great White was seen by day.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiashen, Venus appeared in daylight.

literal: Investigating, Liu Xiang’s "Five Eras Treatise" says, "Great White is lesser yin, weak, cannot go alone; therefore taking jiwei as the limit, it may not thread the sky and travel.
idiomatic: Note Liu Xiang’s "Treatise on the Five Eras": Venus is minor yin and too faint to move independently, so within certain bounds it must not cross the meridian and traverse the full sky.

literal: If it threads the sky then it is seen by day; its prognostications are for weapons and mourning, for disloyal ministers, for changing kings;
idiomatic: When it crosses the zenith it becomes a daytime apparition, portending warfare and mourning, rebellious subjects, and dynastic turnover;

literal: Strong states weaken; small states strengthen.
idiomatic: Great powers decline while lesser polities rise.

literal: " At that time Sun Quan received Wei noble rank, yet raised arms and held out in defense.
idiomatic: At the same time Sun Quan accepted Wei ennoblement while still mobilizing troops in defiance.

literal: That twelfth month, bingzi, the moon offended the great star of Heart.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, the moon again transgressed the principal star of Heart.

literal: The prognostication is the same as above.
idiomatic: The same divination gloss applies as before.

literal: Fifth year, tenth month, yimao, Great White was seen by day.
idiomatic: In the fifth year, tenth month, on yimao, Venus appeared in daylight.

literal: The prognostication is the same as above.
idiomatic: The same divination gloss applies as before.

literal: Further, the Year Star entered Taiwei retrograde, accumulating one hundred forty-nine days then exiting.
idiomatic: Moreover, Jupiter entered the Supreme Palace enclosure in retrograde motion and remained there one hundred forty-nine days before leaving.

literal: The prognostication says, "When the five stars enter Taiwei, entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the human lord has great worry.
idiomatic: The text states, "If the five planets enter the Supreme Palace enclosure from the right and remain thirty days or more, the ruler faces grave peril.

literal: " One gloss says, "A grant of amnesty will arrive.
idiomatic: Another reading adds, "A general amnesty is impending.

literal: " In the seventh year, fifth month, the emperor died; Emperor Ming ascended the throne and granted a great amnesty to all under Heaven.
idiomatic: In the seventh year’s fifth month the emperor died; Emperor Ming succeeded and proclaimed a universal amnesty.

literal: Sixth year, fifth month, renxu, Sparkling Deluder entered Taiwei; reaching renshen it drew level with the Year Star; both offended the Right Law Enforcer; reaching guiyou it then departed.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year, on renxu, Mars entered the Supreme Palace enclosure; by renshen it closed on Jupiter; both transgressed the Right Law Enforcer star; they cleared the region by guiyou.

literal: The prognostication says, "Entering from the right thirty days or more, the human lord has great worry.
idiomatic: The gloss reads, "A right-hand ingress lasting thirty days or more foretells grave danger for the ruler.

literal: " It also says, "When the moon or five planets offend the Left or Right Law Enforcer, great ministers have worry.
idiomatic: It adds, "Lunar or planetary transits across the Left or Right Law Enforcer augur anxiety for senior ministers.

literal: " One gloss says, "Law enforcers are executed; metal and fire are especially severe.
idiomatic: Another line warns, "Officials charged with justice face execution; Venus and Mars make the omen harshest.

literal: " In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, died.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, an imperial son, died.

literal: Seventh year, first month, Cavalry-in-Attendant General Cao Hong was dismissed to commoner status.
idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

literal: Fourth month, South-Conquering Grand General Xiahou Shang died.
idiomatic: In the fourth month Grand General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang died.

literal: Fifth month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor died.

literal: The "Shu Record" states that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan, saying, "The realm stands tripod-like; which region holds the true mandate?
idiomatic: The Shu Record reports Emperor Ming asking Huang Quan which of the three rival states possessed the legitimate cosmic alignment.

literal: " He answered, "One should verify it against celestial patterns.
idiomatic: Huang Quan replied that the answer lay in inspecting the heavens.

literal: " Formerly Sparkling Deluder guarded Heart and Emperor Wen died, yet Wu and Shu had no incident; this is its sign.
idiomatic: He cited Mars stationing at Heart when Emperor Wen died while Wu and Shu remained unscathed as the relevant precedent.

literal: " Investigating the Three Kingdoms histories, there is no text of Sparkling Deluder guarding Heart; it is suspected to mean entering Taiwei.
idiomatic: Scrutiny shows no record of Mars actually stationing at Heart; the event was likely Mars entering the Supreme Palace enclosure.

literal: Eighth month, Wu then besieged Jiangxia, raided Xiangyang; Grand General the Lord of Xuan rescued Xiangyang, beheaded Wu generals including Zhang Ba: this matches weapons-loss and king-change.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Wu besieged Jiangxia and struck Xiangyang; the Lord of Xuan led relief, slew Wu commanders such as Zhang Ba—fulfilling the omen of war, mourning, and shifting supremacy.

literal: Emperor Ming, Taihe fifth year, fifth month, Sparkling Deluder offended Chamber.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth Taihe year of Emperor Ming, Mars transgressed the Chamber mansion.

literal: The prognostication says, "Chamber’s four stars are the thigh-and-arm ministers and the chancellor’s phase; when the moon or five planets offend or guard them, generals and chancellors have worry.
idiomatic: The gloss identifies Chamber’s four stars with the sovereign’s chief ministers; lunar or planetary transits there threaten those officers.

literal: " That seventh month, Chariots-and-Horses General Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was killed by Liang.
idiomatic: In the seventh month General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang He died pursuing Zhuge Liang.

literal: Twelfth month, Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.

literal: That eleventh month, yiyou, the moon offended the great star of Xuanyuan.
idiomatic: In the same eleventh month, on yiyou, the moon transgressed the principal star of Xuanyuan (Regulus).

literal: The prognostication says, "The chief consort has worry.
idiomatic: The text foretells trouble for the empress or chief consort.

literal: " Sixth year, third month, yihai, the moon again offended the great star of Xuanyuan.
idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year, on yihai, the moon again transgressed Regulus.

literal: Eleventh month, yin day, Great White was seen by day in Southern Dipper; it then lasted more than eighty days, constantly seen.
idiomatic: On the yin day of the eleventh month Venus stood in daylight within the Southern Dipper and remained visible more than eighty consecutive days.

literal: The prognostication says, "Wu has weapons.
idiomatic: The gloss predicts military action involving Wu.

literal: " Next year Sun Quan sent Zhang Mi and others leading ten thousand troops to invest Gongsun Wenyi as King of Yan; Wenyi slew Mi and seized his host.
idiomatic: The following year Sun Quan dispatched Zhang Mi with ten thousand men to enfeoff Gongsun Yuan as King of Yan; Yuan executed the envoys and captured the army.

literal: Blue Dragon third year, first month, Empress Dowager Guo died.
idiomatic: In the first month of the third Blue Dragon year Empress Dowager Guo died.

literal: Blue Dragon third year, third month, xinmao, the moon offended Ghost Carriage.
idiomatic: In the third month of the third Blue Dragon year, on xinmao, the moon transgressed the Ghost asterism.

literal: Ghost Carriage governs beheading and killing.
idiomatic: The Ghost asterism presides over executions and slaughter.

literal: The prognostication says, "Many people fall ill; the state has worry.
idiomatic: It warns of widespread sickness and national anxiety.

literal: " It also says, "Great ministers have worry.
idiomatic: A second reading adds peril for high ministers.

literal: " That year, summer and winter, great pestilence.
idiomatic: That summer and winter a severe epidemic raged.

literal: Fourth year, fifth month, Minister of Education Dong Zhao died.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year Minister over the Masses Dong Zhao died.

literal: That fifth month, dinghai, Great White was seen by day, accumulating more than thirty days.
idiomatic: In the same fifth month, on dinghai, Venus shone in daylight for over thirty days.

literal: By gnomon-shadow degrees extrapolating it, it was not Qin or Wei, then it was Chu.
idiomatic: Shadow-rod reckoning assigned the omen to the Chu sector rather than Qin or Wei heartlands.

literal: At that time Zhuge Liang held south of the Wei River and the Lord of Xuan faced him in stalemate;
idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was entrenched south of the Wei while the Lord of Xuan contained him;

literal: Sun Quan raided Hefei and also sent Lu Yi, Sun Shao, and others into the Huai and Han rivers; the Son of Heaven personally campaigned east.
idiomatic: Sun Quan struck at Hefei and sent Lu Yi, Sun Shao, and others into the Huai-Han basin, prompting an eastern expedition by the emperor.

literal: Shu is fundamentally Qin territory, so Qin, Wei, and Chu arms all rose together.
idiomatic: Because Shu occupied the old Qin domain, the omen materialized as simultaneous warfare across the Qin, Wei, and Chu astrological divisions.

literal: That seventh month, jisi, the moon offended Key-and-Bar.
idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jisi, the moon transgressed the Key-and-Bar stars.

literal: The prognostication says, "There is fire disaster.
idiomatic: The gloss portends conflagration.

literal: " Third year, seventh month, the Chonghua Palace burned.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year the Chonghua Palace caught fire.

literal: Third year, sixth month, dingwei, Station Star offended Well’s axe-star.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, on dingwei, Saturn transgressed the axe star of Eastern Well.

literal: On wuxu, Great White again offended it.
idiomatic: On wuxu Venus likewise transgressed that star.

literal: The prognostication says, "Whenever the moon or five planets offend Well’s axe, all mean weapon disaster.
idiomatic: The text states that lunar or planetary hits on the Well axe-star always presage military calamity.

literal: " One gloss says, "Axes and halberds are used; great ministers are executed.
idiomatic: Another line warns of capital punishment falling on senior officials.

literal: " Seventh month, jichou, Station Star offended Eastern Well’s separation star.
idiomatic: On jichou of the seventh month Saturn transgressed the separation star of Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication says, "When Station Star enters Well, great men have worry.
idiomatic: Saturn entering the Well mansion augurs anxiety for high lords.

literal: " Moving near the separation star counts as traveling the yin aspect.
idiomatic: Passing close to the separation star is interpreted as motion along the yin side of the lodge.

literal: Its prognostication says, "Great flood; the five grains do not ripen.
idiomatic: The associated reading predicts catastrophic flooding and crop failure.

literal: " Jingchu first year, summer, great flood, injuring the five grains.
idiomatic: In the first Jingchu summer floods ruined the harvest.

literal: That year, tenth month, renshen, Great White was seen by day, in Tail, lasting more than two hundred days, constantly seen by day.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, on renshen, Venus appeared in daylight in the Tail mansion and remained a daytime object for over two hundred days.

literal: The prognostication says, "Tail is Yan; there are weapons.
idiomatic: Tail corresponds to the Yan region and foretells war.

literal: " Twelfth month, wuchen, the moon offended Hook-and-Lock.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuchen, the moon transgressed the Hook-and-Lock stars.

literal: The prognostication says, "The king has worry.
idiomatic: The king himself is said to face peril.

literal: " Fourth year, intercalary first month, jisi, Station Star offended Well’s axe.
idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the fourth year, on jisi, Saturn again transgressed the Well axe-star.

literal: Third month, guimao, Station Star offended Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the third month, on guimao, Saturn transgressed Eastern Well.

literal: On jisi, Great White together with the Moon, brightness added to the solar glare, were seen by day.
idiomatic: On jisi Venus and the Moon were visible in daylight, their brilliance heightened against the sunlit sky.

literal: Fifth month, renyin, Great White offended the first star of Net’s left thigh.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renyin, Venus transgressed the first star along the left thigh of the Net mansion.

literal: The prognostication says, "Net is border weapons; it also governs punishments.
idiomatic: Net presides over frontier warfare and judicial punishments.

literal: " Ninth month, beyond the passes in Liangzhou the Hu chieftain Abi Shi envoys raided the states; Colonel of the Western Regions Zhang Jiu campaigned, beheading and capturing on the order of ten thousand.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Liangzhou frontier Hu led by Abi Shi’s envoys attacked neighboring states; Colonel of the Western Regions Zhang Jiu crushed them, taking tens of thousands of heads and captives.

literal: That year, seventh month, jiayin, Great White offended the great star of Xuanyuan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year, on jiayin, Venus transgressed Regulus.

literal: The prognostication says, "The chief consort has worry.
idiomatic: The omen again targets the chief consort.

literal: " Jingchu first year, Empress Mao died.
idiomatic: In the first Jingchu year Empress Mao died.

literal: Jingchu first year, second month, yiyou, the moon offended the second star of Chamber.
idiomatic: In the first Jingchu year, second month, on yiyou, the moon transgressed the second star of Chamber.

literal: The prognostication says, "Generals have worry.
idiomatic: The gloss warns of danger to generals.

literal: " That seventh month, Minister of Education Chen Jiao died.
idiomatic: In the seventh month Minister over the Masses Chen Jiao died.

literal: Second year, fourth month, Minister of Education Han Ji died.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Minister over the Masses Han Ji died.

literal: That seventh month, xinmao, Great White was seen by day, accumulating more than two hundred eighty days.
idiomatic: In the seventh month, on xinmao, Venus remained a daytime object for over two hundred eighty days.

literal: At that time Gongsun Wenyi had declared himself King of Yan, appointed officials at will, raised troops and held defense; the Lord of Xuan campaigned and destroyed him.
idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan had styled himself King of Yan, set up a full bureaucracy, and resisted; the Lord of Xuan extirpated the regime.

literal: Second year, second month, jichou, the moon offended Heart’s separation star and also offended the central great star.
idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, on jichou, the moon transgressed Heart’s separation star and the central principal star.

literal: Fifth month, yihai, the moon again offended Heart’s separation star and the central great star.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yihai, the moon repeated those transits across Heart.

literal: Investigating, the prognostication says, "The king abhors it.
idiomatic: The compiled gloss states that the sovereign should dread such alignments.

literal: Offending the front star, the heir apparent has worry.
idiomatic: Striking the anterior star augurs trouble for the heir apparent.

literal: " Third year, first month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the emperor died.

literal: The heir was enthroned but in the end was deposed.
idiomatic: The new heir ascended yet was ultimately cast down.

literal: That year, tenth month, jiawu, the moon offended Winnowing-Basket.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, on jiawu, the moon transgressed Winnowing-Basket.

literal: The prognostication says, "The general dies.
idiomatic: The reading predicts a general’s death.

literal: " Zhengshi first year, fourth month, Chariots-and-Horses General Huang Quan died.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first Zhengshi year General of Chariots and Cavalry Huang Quan died.

literal: That intercalary eleventh month, guichou, the moon offended Heart’s central great star.
idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month, on guichou, the moon transgressed the central great star of Heart.

literal: Young Emperor Zhengshi first year, fourth month, wuwu, the moon offended the first eastern star of Hairy Head.
idiomatic: In the first Zhengshi year of the young emperor, fourth month, wuwu, the moon transgressed the leading eastern star of the Hairy Head cluster.

literal: Tenth month, gengyin, the moon again offended Hairy Head and the fourth star of Northern Dipper.
idiomatic: In the tenth month, on gengyin, the moon again transgressed the Pleiades region and the fourth star of the Northern Dipper.

literal: The prognostication says, "When the moon offends Hairy Head, the Hu are not settled.
idiomatic: A lunar hit on Hairy Head unsettles the northern frontier peoples.

literal: " Second year, sixth month, Xianbei under Amiao’er and others raided the west; Dunhuang Prefect Wang Yan defeated them, beheading more than twenty thousand ranks.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year Xianbei bands led by Amiao’er struck westward; Prefect of Dunhuang Wang Yan routed them, taking over twenty thousand heads.

literal: Third year, again beheaded the Xianbei grand shaman and more than a thousand ranks.
idiomatic: In the third year another campaign slew the Xianbei grand shaman and over a thousand others.

literal: Second year, ninth month, guiyou, the moon offended Ghost’s northwest star.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year, on guiyou, the moon transgressed the northwest star of Ghost.

literal: Third year, second month, dingwei, again offended the southwest star.
idiomatic: In the third year’s second month, on dingwei, it again transgressed the southwest star of Ghost.

literal: The prognostication says, "There is a money edict.
idiomatic: One reading speaks of a monetary ordinance or cash distribution.

literal: " One gloss says, "Great ministers have worry.
idiomatic: Another gloss still warns of anxiety for senior ministers.

literal: " Third year, third month, Grand Commandant Man Chong died.
idiomatic: In the third month of the third year Grand Commandant Man Chong died.

literal: Fourth year, first month, the emperor assumed the capped-age rite and bestowed cash on the various ministers in graded amounts.
idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the emperor came of age ceremonially and granted sums of money to officials in graded gifts.

literal: Fourth year, tenth and eleventh months, the moon twice offended Well’s axe.
idiomatic: In the tenth and eleventh months of the fourth year the moon twice transgressed the Well axe-star.

literal: That month the Lord of Xuan campaigned against Zhuge Ke; Ke abandoned the city and fled.
idiomatic: That same month the Lord of Xuan attacked Zhuge Ke, who fled abandoning his city.

literal: Fifth year, second month, Cao Shuang campaigned against Shu.
idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year Cao Shuang invaded Shu.

literal: Fifth year, eleventh month, guisi, Station Star offended Neck’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifth year, on guisi, Saturn transgressed the separation star of the Neck mansion.

literal: The prognostication says, "Among the feudal lords there are those who lose their state.
idiomatic: The gloss foretells feudal lords stripped of their domains.

literal: " Seventh year, seventh month, dingchou, the moon offended the left Horn.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year, on dingchou, the moon transgressed the left Horn star.

literal: The prognostication says, "Under Heaven there are weapons; the left general dies.
idiomatic: It predicts war across the realm and death for a general of the left.

literal: " Seventh month, yihai, Sparkling Deluder offended Net’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the seventh month, on yihai, Mars transgressed the separation star of Net.

literal: The prognostication says;
idiomatic: The prognostication text continues:

literal: "There is border weapons.
idiomatic: "Border warfare will erupt.

literal: " One gloss says, "Punishments are applied.
idiomatic: A variant reading adds widespread use of criminal justice.

literal: " Ninth year, first month, xinhai, the moon offended Neck’s southern star.
idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year, on xinhai, the moon transgressed the southern star of Neck.

literal: The prognostication says, "Weapons arise.
idiomatic: The omen signals the outbreak of arms.

literal: " One gloss says, "The general dies.
idiomatic: Another line again predicts a commander’s death.

literal: " Seventh month, guichou, Station Star offended Key-and-Bar.
idiomatic: In the seventh month, on guichou, Saturn transgressed Key-and-Bar.

literal: The prognostication says, "The king ought not go out from palace or descend the hall.
idiomatic: The king is warned not to leave the palace or descend the main hall.

literal: " Jiaping first year, the Son of Heaven visited the tombs; the Lord of Xuan memorialized to execute Cao Shuang and others.
idiomatic: In the first Jiaping year the emperor performed tomb rites while the Lord of Xuan secured an order to execute Cao Shuang’s faction.

literal: The Son of Heaven lodged in the field; thereby he lost power.
idiomatic: The emperor was forced to encamp abroad and thereafter forfeited real authority.

literal: Jiaping first year, sixth month, renxu, Great White offended Eastern Well’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first Jiaping year, on renxu, Venus transgressed the separation star of Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication says, "The state loses governance; great ministers make rebellion.
idiomatic: The text foretells misrule at court and ministerial revolt.

literal: " Fourth month, xinsi, Great White offended Ghost Carriage.
idiomatic: In the fourth month, on xinsi, Venus transgressed the Ghost asterism.

literal: The prognostication says, "Great ministers are beheaded.
idiomatic: Senior ministers face execution.

literal: " One gloss says, "Weapons arise.
idiomatic: An alternate reading again predicts war.

literal: " Second year, third month, jiwei, Great White again offended Well’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, on jiwei, Venus again transgressed the Well separation star.

literal: Third year, seventh month, Wang Ling and Prince Biao of Chu plotted; all were executed; the human lord thereafter was humbled.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year Wang Ling and Cao Biao, Prince of Chu, were exposed and executed, greatly diminishing the throne’s stature.

literal: Wu: Sun Quan, Red Crow thirteenth year, summer, fifth month, sun reached northernmost; Sparkling Deluder retrograded and entered Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: In Wu, the thirteenth Red Crow year, the summer fifth month at the summer solstice, Mars turned retrograde and entered the Southern Dipper.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, it offended the third star of the Dipper’s ladle then moved east.
idiomatic: By autumn’s seventh month it transgressed the third star of the dipper’s bowl and proceeded eastward.

literal: The "Han-Jin Spring and Autumn" says "retrograde motion."
idiomatic: Han-Jin Spring and Autumn explicitly labels the motion as retrograde.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "When Sparkling Deluder enters Southern Dipper, within three months the Wu king dies.
idiomatic: Compiled lore states that Mars in the Southern Dipper foretells the Wu ruler’s death within three months.

literal: " One gloss says, "When Sparkling Deluder retrogrades, that region has a dead lord.
idiomatic: Retrograde Mars over a territory likewise augurs a ruler’s death.

literal: " Taikang second year, Quan died; this matched it, therefore the "National Records" place the entry under Wu.
idiomatic: Sun Quan died in the second Taikang year, matching the omen, so the National Records assign the observation to Wu.

literal: At that time Wang Ling plotted to enthrone Prince Biao of Chu, saying, "There is a star in the Dipper—surely someone will rise to sudden eminence," and questioned the star-knower Hao Xiang.
idiomatic: Wang Ling, scheming to elevate Prince Biao, cited an unusual star in the Dipper as a sign of sudden greatness and consulted Hao Xiang.

literal: Xiang suspected hidden motives and, wishing to please him, did not speak of Wu’s mourning but said, "Huainan is Chu allotment; Wu and Chu share the same reading—there ought to be a king who rises," so Ling’s plan firmed.
idiomatic: Hao Xiang, doubting Wang Ling’s purpose, avoided predicting Wu’s bereavement and instead claimed Huainan’s Chu sector meant a new king would arise, which hardened Ling’s resolve.

literal: Jiaping second year, twelfth month, bingshen, the moon offended Ghost Carriage.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second Jiaping year, on bingshen, the moon transgressed Ghost.

literal: Third year, fourth month, wuyin, the moon offended Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, on wuyin, the moon transgressed Eastern Well.

literal: Fifth month, jiayin, the moon offended Neck’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin, the moon transgressed Neck’s separation star.

literal: The prognostication says, "The general dies.
idiomatic: The gloss again predicts a commander’s death.

literal: " One gloss says, "There will be arms.
idiomatic: Another reading simply foretells warfare.

literal: " That month Wang Ling, Prince Biao of Chu, and others were executed.
idiomatic: That month Wang Ling, Prince Biao, and their confederates were put to death.

literal: Seventh month, Empress Zhen died.
idiomatic: In the seventh month Empress Zhen died.

literal: Fourth year, third month, Wu generals raided; Area Commander East Zhuge Dan routed them.
idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year Wu commanders invaded; General Who Guards the East Zhuge Dan drove them off.

literal: That year, seventh month, jisi, the moon offended Ghost Carriage.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year, on jisi, the moon transgressed Ghost.

literal: Ninth month, yisi, again offended it.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yisi, it transgressed Ghost again.

literal: Tenth month, guiwei, Sparkling Deluder offended Neck’s southern star.
idiomatic: In the tenth month, on guiwei, Mars transgressed Neck’s southern star.

literal: The prognostication says, "Ministers have rebellion.
idiomatic: The text warns of mutiny among ministers.

literal: " Fourth year, eleventh month, dingwei, the moon again offended Ghost’s piled corpses.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, on dingwei, the moon again transgressed the heaped-corpse cluster in Ghost.

literal: Fifth year, sixth month, wuwu, Great White offended Horn.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year, on wuwu, Venus transgressed the Horn mansion.

literal: The prognostication says, "The various ministers plot but do not succeed.
idiomatic: Courtiers intrigue yet fail to carry a coup through.

literal: " Gengchen, the moon offended Winnowing-Basket star.
idiomatic: On gengchen the moon transgressed a star in Winnowing-Basket.

literal: The prognostication says, "The general dies.
idiomatic: Another death omen for generals follows.

literal: " Seventh month, the moon offended Well’s axe.
idiomatic: In the seventh month the moon transgressed the Well axe-star.

literal: Bingwu, the moon again offended Ghost’s northwest star.
idiomatic: On bingwu the moon again transgressed Ghost’s northwest star.

literal: The prognostication says, "The state has worry.
idiomatic: The state faces grave concern.

literal: " Eleventh month, guiyou, the moon offended Eastern Well’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guiyou, the moon transgressed Eastern Well’s separation star.

literal: The prognostication says, "The general dies.
idiomatic: The gloss again predicts a general’s death.

literal: " Zhengyuan first year, first month, Area Commander East Guanqiu Jian and Inspector of Yang Province Wen Qin rebelled; both hosts were defeated and they were executed.
idiomatic: In the first month of the first Zhengyuan year General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Inspector of Yang Province Wen Qin rose in revolt, lost their armies, and were executed.

literal: Second month, Li Feng, his brother Yi, the empress’s father Zhang Ji, and others plotted rebellion; the affair leaked; all were executed; Empress Zhang was deposed.
idiomatic: In the second month Li Feng, Li Yi, Empress Zhang’s father Zhang Ji, and others conspired; exposed, they were slain and Empress Zhang was cast aside.

literal: Ninth month, the emperor was deposed as Prince of Qi.
idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor was demoted to Prince of Qi.

literal: Shu general Jiang Wei attacked Longxi; Chariots-and-Horses General Guo Huai campaigned and defeated him.
idiomatic: Shu’s Jiang Wei struck Longxi; General of Chariots and Cavalry Guo Huai repulsed him.

literal: Duke of Gaoxiang, Zhengyuan second year, second month, wuwu, Sparkling Deluder offended the first western star at the northern yoke-head of Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the second Zhengyuan year of the Duke of Gaoxiang, second month, wuwu, Mars transgressed the leading western star on the northern yoke of Eastern Well.

literal: Ganlu first year, seventh month, yimao, Sparkling Deluder offended Eastern Well’s axe-star.
idiomatic: In the first Ganlu year, seventh month, on yimao, Mars transgressed the Well axe-star.

literal: Renxu, the moon again offended the axe-star.
idiomatic: On renxu the moon again transgressed the axe-star.

literal: Eighth month, xinhai, the moon offended Winnowing-Basket.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai, the moon transgressed Winnowing-Basket.

literal: Wu deposed Sun Liang: Taiping first year, ninth month, renchen, Great White offended Southern Dipper, as the Wu Annals record.
idiomatic: When Wu deposed Sun Liang, in the first Taiping year’s ninth month, on renchen, Venus transgressed the Southern Dipper—the entry appears in the Wu Annals.

literal: The prognostication says, "When Great White offends the Dipper, the state has weapons; great ministers have rebels.
idiomatic: Venus striking the Dipper presages war and treason among great ministers.

literal: " The next year Zhuge Dan rebelled.
idiomatic: The following year Zhuge Dan rose in rebellion.

literal: Again the next year Sun Chen deposed Liang.
idiomatic: The year after that Sun Chen removed Sun Liang.

literal: Wu and Wei together had military affairs.
idiomatic: Both Wu and Wei saw major campaigning.

literal: Ganlu first year, ninth month, dingsi, the moon offended Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the first Ganlu year’s ninth month, on dingsi, the moon transgressed Eastern Well.

literal: Second year, sixth month, jiyou, the moon offended Heart’s central great star.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year, on jiyou, the moon transgressed Heart’s central great star.

literal: Eighth month, renzi, the Year Star offended Well’s axe.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, Jupiter transgressed the Well axe-star.

literal: Ninth month, gengyin, the Year Star retrograded, riding atop Well’s axe.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Jupiter moved retrograde across the Well axe-star.

literal: Tenth month, bingyin, Great White offended Neck’s separation star.
idiomatic: In the tenth month, on bingyin, Venus transgressed Neck’s separation star.

literal: The prognostication says, "Rebellious ministers make chaos; the human lord worries.
idiomatic: Rebellious subjects stir turmoil and the ruler faces anxiety.

literal: " Jingyuan first year, fifth month, the Cheng Ji incident and Zhuge Dan’s execution—all were its correspondences.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first Jingyuan year the Cheng Ji coup and Zhuge Dan’s liquidation fulfilled these omens.

literal: Second year, third month, gengzi, Great White offended Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, on gengzi, Venus transgressed Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication says, "The state loses governance; great ministers make rebellion.
idiomatic: The same gloss of misrule and ministerial revolt applies.

literal: " That night, the Year Star again offended Eastern Well.
idiomatic: That same night Jupiter again transgressed Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication says, "Weapons arise.
idiomatic: The reading again signals war.

literal: " Reaching Jingyuan first year, the Duke of Gaoxiang was defeated.
idiomatic: By the first Jingyuan year the Duke of Gaoxiang had been overthrown.

literal: Third year, eighth month, renchen, the Year Star offended Ghost’s execution-blade star.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, on renchen, Jupiter transgressed the execution-blade star in Ghost.

literal: The prognostication says, "Axes and execution-blades are used; great ministers are beheaded.
idiomatic: Capital punishment falls on high officials when this star is struck.

literal: " Fourth year, fourth month, jiashen, the Year Star again offended Ghost’s southeast star.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, on jiashen, Jupiter again transgressed Ghost’s southeast star.

literal: The prognostication says, "Ghost’s southeast star governs weapons; when wood enters Ghost, great ministers are beheaded.
idiomatic: The southeast star of Ghost rules military affairs; Jupiter entering Ghost beheads ministers.

literal: " Jingyuan first year, they killed Minister Wang Jing.
idiomatic: In the first Jingyuan year Minister Wang Jing was executed.

literal: Prince of Wei, Jingyuan first year, second month, the moon offended Establishment Stars.
idiomatic: In the second month of the first Jingyuan year of the Wei prince, the moon transgressed the Establishment asterism.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "When the moon or five planets offend Establishment Stars, great ministers slander one another.
idiomatic: Compiled lore states that lunar or planetary hits on the Establishment stars pit chief ministers against each other through slander.

literal: " Afterward Zhong Hui and Deng Ai destroyed Shu; Hui slandered Ai.
idiomatic: Later Zhong Hui and Deng Ai conquered Shu, whereupon Hui denounced Ai.

literal: Second year, fourth month, Sparkling Deluder entered Taiwei and offended the Right Law Enforcer.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Mars entered the Supreme Palace enclosure and transgressed the Right Law Enforcer.

literal: The prognostication says, "The human lord has great worry.
idiomatic: The ruler faces supreme peril.

literal: " One version says, "Great ministers worry.
idiomatic: Another manuscript reads anxiety for great ministers instead.

literal: " Fourth year, tenth month, the Year Star guarded Chamber.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year Jupiter stationed at Chamber.

literal: The prognostication says, "Generals and chancellors worry.
idiomatic: Generals and chancellors face danger.

literal: " One version says, "There is a great amnesty.
idiomatic: An alternate gloss promises a sweeping pardon.

literal: " Next year Deng Ai and Zhong Hui were both exterminated and Shu territory was amnestied.
idiomatic: The next year Deng Ai and Zhong Hui were annihilated and the Shu lands received clemency.

literal: Fifth year, the emperor yielded the throne.
idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor abdicated.

literal: Emperor Wu, Xianning fourth year, ninth month, Great White ought to have appeared but did not appear.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth Xianning year of Emperor Wu, Venus should have been visible but failed to appear.
